q.s: Which Harappan site in India was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2021?
q.x: Dholavira in Gujarat was inscribed in 2021; Rakhigarhi is not on the World Heritage List.

q.s: Which Harappan site was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site as early as 1980?
q.x: Mohenjodaro (now in Pakistan) was inscribed in 1980; Harappa is not inscribed.

q.s: The weapons of the early Vedic tribal militia (Sena) were mainly made of:
q.x: Early Vedic weapons were of copper and bronze; iron came into use only in the Later Vedic age.

q.s: In the Vedic period, the union of a childless widow with her husband's brother was called:
q.x: Niyoga was the levirate union; swayamvara was a girl's choice of husband in an open assembly.

q.s: Which of the following statements about women in the Rigvedic period is correct?
o: Women could choose their husbands and attend assemblies.
Niyoga meant a girl's choice of husband in an open assembly.
Polygamy was the usual form of marriage.
Their position improved further in the Later Vedic period.
q.x: Rigvedic women could choose husbands and attend assemblies; monogamy was the norm and their position declined in the Later Vedic period.

q.s: Among the ratnins of the Later Vedic king, the Sangrahitri was the:
q.x: The Sangrahitri was the treasurer; the Senani was army chief, the Suta charioteer and the Akshavapa superintendent of dice.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the ratnins of the Later Vedic king?
q.x: Senani, Suta and Bhagadugha (tax collector) were ratnins; Amatya is a later (Mauryan/Arthashastra) term.

q.s: Who carried a branch of the Bodhi tree to Sri Lanka in Ashoka's time?
q.x: Sanghamitta, Ashoka's daughter, took the Bodhi branch; Mahinda led the mission received by Devanampiya Tissa.

q.s: Ashoka's missionaries Sona and Uttara were sent to:
q.x: Sona and Uttara went to Suvarnabhumi; Majjhantika went to Kashmir and Gandhara, Maharakkhita to the Yavana country.

q.s: Which Mauryan tax was paid only in cash?
q.x: Hiranya was paid in cash; bhaga was the share of produce and pindakara was assessed on groups of villages.

q.s: The Kanva dynasty was founded by:
q.x: Vasudeva Kanva killed Devabhuti, the last Sunga, and founded the Kanva line.

q.s: The last Kanva ruler, Susharman, was overthrown by the:
q.x: The Satavahanas ended Kanva rule; four Kanva kings ruled c. 73-28 BC.

q.s: The first Huna attack on the Gupta empire was checked by:
q.x: The first Huna attack, at the end of Kumaragupta I's reign, was repulsed by prince Skandagupta.

q.s: The Huna ruler Mihirakula was the son of:
q.x: Mihirakula succeeded his father Toramana, who had conquered up to Eran.

q.s: In the Gupta town board (adhikarana), the Sarthavaha represented the:
q.x: Sarthavaha was the chief caravan trader; the Nagarashreshthi (chief banker) chaired the board.

q.s: The Prayaga Prashasti, recording the achievements of Samudragupta, was composed by:
q.x: Harishena, Samudragupta's court poet, composed it; Ravikirti wrote the Aihole inscription of Pulakeshin II.

q.s: The largest hoard of Gupta coins has been found at:
q.x: The Bayana hoard in Rajasthan is the largest find of Gupta coins.

q.s: Gupta silver coinage was first issued by:
q.x: Chandragupta II began silver coins on the Saka model after conquering the Western Kshatrapas.

q.s: In the battle of Takkolam (949 CE), the Rashtrakuta king Krishna III defeated the Chola king:
q.x: At Takkolam Krishna III defeated Parantaka I, a major setback for the early Cholas.

q.s: The Brihadeeswara (Rajarajeswara) temple at Thanjavur was built by:
q.x: Rajaraja I completed the Thanjavur temple in 1010.

q.s: Gangaikondacholapuram was founded as the Chola capital by:
q.x: Rajendra I built it after his campaign to the Ganga, taking the title Gangaikonda.

q.s: In Chola inscriptions, 'Shalabhoga' land was meant for the maintenance of:
q.x: Shalabhoga was land for a school; devadana went to temples, pallichchandam to Jaina institutions and eripatti to the tank.

q.s: During the Mongol siege of Delhi in 1303, Alauddin Khalji took shelter in the fort of:
q.x: Alauddin camped at Siri; Tughlaqabad was built later by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.

q.s: Alauddin Khalji met the Mongol threat mainly by:
q.x: He raised a large standing army paid in cash and repaired the north-western forts.

q.s: Ibn Battuta, who came to India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq, was a native of:
q.x: Ibn Battuta was born at Tangiers in Morocco and reached India in 1333.

q.s: Muhammad bin Tughlaq appointed Ibn Battuta as Qazi of Delhi and later sent him as his envoy to:
q.x: In 1342 the Sultan sent him as his envoy to the Mongol emperor of China.

q.s: Timur invaded India in 1398 during the reign of:
q.x: Timur sacked Delhi in December 1398 under the last Tughlaq, Nasiruddin Mahmud; Ibrahim Lodi fell to Babur in 1526.

q.s: The dynasty that came to power in Delhi soon after Timur's invasion was the:
q.x: Khizr Khan, Timur's nominee, founded the Sayyid dynasty in 1414.

q.s: Khazain-ul-Futuh, an account of Alauddin Khalji's campaigns, was written by:
q.x: Amir Khusrau wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh; Isami wrote Futuh-us-Salatin.

q.s: Which of the following works was NOT written by Amir Khusrau?
q.x: Futuh-us-Salatin is by Abdul Malik Isami; the other three are Khusrau's.

q.s: Addanki Gangadhara, the first to dedicate a Telugu work to a Muslim ruler, dedicated 'Tapati Samvaranopakhyanam' to:
q.x: It was dedicated to Ibrahim Qutb Shah (Malki Bharama), a patron of Telugu.

q.s: Suraj Mal, called 'the Plato of the Jat tribe', ruled the Jat state of:
q.x: Badan Singh founded the Jat state of Bharatpur; Suraj Mal (1755-63) was its greatest ruler.

q.s: The Satnami revolt of 1672 against Aurangzeb broke out at:
q.x: The Satnamis of Narnaul rose in 1672; Guru Ghasidas belongs to the 19th century.

q.s: The 'du-aspa sih-aspa' rank in the Mughal mansab system was introduced by:
q.x: Jahangir introduced it, counting part of the sawar double without raising the zat.

q.s: In the Mughal administration, the news-writers (waqia-navis) and harkaras worked under the:
q.x: The Mir Bakhshi headed the military department and the intelligence service.

q.s: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa in 1699 at:
q.x: The Khalsa was founded at Anandpur on Baisakhi 1699 with the baptism of the Panj Pyare.

q.s: Before his death in 1708, Guru Gobind Singh declared as the eternal Guru of the Sikhs:
q.x: He vested Guruship in the Guru Granth Sahib; Banda Bahadur was only his military successor.

q.s: Shah Muhammad Ghaus of Gwalior belonged to which Sufi order?
q.x: Shah Muhammad Ghaus was a leading Shattari saint.

q.s: Mughal prince Dara Shikoh was a follower of which Sufi order?
q.x: Dara Shikoh was a disciple of Mulla Shah Badakhshi of the Qadiri order.

q.s: In the Maratha system, 'Saranjam' was:
o: Land assigned to chiefs for military service
q.x: Saranjam was land assigned to Maratha chiefs for maintaining troops.

q.s: Most of the Peshwa Daftar records at Pune are written in the:
q.x: The Peshwa Daftar records are mostly in the cursive Modi script; Elphinstone preserved them after 1818.

q.s: The first Portuguese factory in India was set up by Cabral in 1500 at:
q.x: Cabral set up the first factory at Calicut (1500), followed by trading centres at Cannanore and Cochin.

q.s: Vasco da Gama, who came to India for the third time in 1524 as Viceroy, died at:
q.x: He died at Kochi in 1524, the year of his third voyage.

q.s: The English defeated the Portuguese in the Battle of Swally, near Surat, in:
q.x: Swally (1612) was followed by the defeat off Jask (1620) and the loss of Ormuz (1622).

q.s: The 'cartaz' system introduced by the Portuguese in the Indian Ocean was a:
o: Pass that ships had to buy to trade
q.x: The cartaz was a licence that Asian ships had to carry; it enforced the Portuguese trade monopoly and hurt Calicut's trade.

q.s: The fort of Bobbili was destroyed in 1757 by Vijayaramaraju of Vizianagaram with the help of:
q.x: The French under Bussy joined Vijayaramaraju in the Battle of Bobbili (1757).

q.s: In the Battle of Chandurthi (1758), Col. Forde defeated the French under:
q.x: Forde defeated Conflans; Lally was defeated by Eyre Coote at Wandiwash (1760).

q.s: The first Dutch factory in Andhra was established in 1605 at:
q.x: Machilipatnam (1605) was the first; Nizampatnam followed in 1606 and Draksharama in 1633.

q.s: The Madras Native Association (1852) was founded by:
q.x: Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty founded it; it petitioned against the non-implementation of the Queen's Proclamation.

q.s: The period 1858-1885, when the promises of the Queen's Proclamation were not kept, is called the:
q.x: Promises such as appointment by merit were broken; the ICS stayed European.

q.s: The Third Carnatic War ended with the Treaty of:
q.x: The Third War ended with the Treaty of Paris (1763).

q.s: The First Carnatic War came to an end with the Treaty of:
q.x: Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) ended the First War; the Second ended with Pondicherry (1754-55).

q.s: Under the British 'ring-fence' policy, which state served as a buffer shielding Bengal from the Marathas and Afghans?
q.x: Awadh was the buffer state under the ring-fence policy.

q.s: The first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833 was:
q.x: Bentinck was the last Governor-General of Bengal and the first Governor-General of India.

q.s: Slavery was abolished in India in 1843 during the tenure of:
q.x: The Act of 1843 abolishing slavery came under Ellenborough, not Bentinck.

q.s: The Treaty of Yandabo (1826), ending the First Anglo-Burmese War, was signed during the tenure of:
q.x: Amherst (1823-28) fought the First Burmese War ending with Yandabo.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Governor-General and event is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Treaty of Lahore (1846) was signed under Hardinge I, not Dalhousie.

q.s: The Ryotwari system was first tried in the Baramahal in 1792 by:
q.x: Alexander Read began it in the Baramahal with Thomas Munro as his assistant.

q.s: The Ryotwari system was officially enforced in the whole Madras Presidency in 1820 by:
q.x: Munro, as Governor of Madras, enforced it in 1820; Elphinstone extended it to Bombay.

q.s: India's first jute mill was set up in 1855 at:
q.x: Rishra near Calcutta had the first jute mill; Fort Gloster saw a failed cotton mill attempt in 1818.

q.s: The Assam Company, formed in 1839, was India's first company in the field of:
q.x: The Assam Company (1839) was the first tea company.

q.s: Macaulay's Minute on education (1835) recommended that government funds be spent on:
o: Oriental learning through Sanskrit and Persian
q.x: Macaulay wanted Western learning through English to create a class of interpreters between rulers and ruled.

q.s: Which document is called the 'Magna Carta of English education in India'?
q.x: Wood's Despatch (1854) laid down a comprehensive scheme of education from primary to university.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of Wood's Despatch (1854)?
o: Adoption of the Downward Filtration Theory
q.x: Wood's Despatch rejected, at least on paper, the Downward Filtration Theory.

q.s: The All-India Muslim League was founded in December 1906 at:
q.x: It was founded at Dacca on 30 December 1906; its headquarters was later at Lucknow.

q.s: The first annual session of the Muslim League (1907) was held at:
q.x: The first session met at Karachi (1907) and the second at Amritsar (1908).

q.s: The Moderates who left the Congress over the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms formed the:
q.x: Under Surendranath Banerjee the Moderates formed the Indian Liberal Federation; the Swarajya Party came in 1923 under C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru.

q.s: The Amritsar session of the Congress (1919) was presided over by:
q.x: Motilal Nehru presided; Hasan Imam presided over the special Bombay session of 1918.

q.s: The death of the child bride Phulmoni Dasi led to the passing of the:
q.x: Phulmoni Dasi's death pushed the Age of Consent Act (1891).

q.s: 'Notes on Infant Marriage and Enforced Widowhood' (1884) was written by:
q.x: Behramji Malabari, editor of the Indian Spectator, wrote it.

q.s: The Communal Award of 1932 was announced by the British Prime Minister:
q.x: Ramsay MacDonald announced it on 16 August 1932; Gandhi's fast against it led to the Poona Pact.

q.s: The Poona Pact of September 1932 was an agreement between Gandhi and:
q.x: The Poona Pact gave reserved seats to the depressed classes within joint electorates instead of separate electorates.

q.s: The first principal of the Besant Theosophical College, Madanapalle, was:
q.x: James H. Cousins was its first principal.

q.s: Which journal of the Ramakrishna movement was published in English?
q.x: Prabuddha Bharata was the English journal; Udbodhan was in Bengali.

q.s: Swami Vivekananda founded the Vedanta Society of New York in:
q.x: He founded it in 1894, a year after the Chicago Parliament of Religions.

q.s: The Darul Uloom at Deoband was founded in 1866 by Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi and:
q.x: Nanautavi and Gangohi founded it in 1866; 1875 is the year of Sir Syed's Aligarh college.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Deoband school is correct?
o: It was founded in 1875 in Aligarh.
In 1888 it supported Sir Syed's United Patriotic Association.
It aimed mainly to spread Western education among Muslims.
It welcomed the Indian National Congress.
q.x: Deoband welcomed the Congress and issued a fatwa against Sir Syed's United Patriotic Association in 1888.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT an aim of the Deoband school?
o: Propagating the pure teachings of the Quran and Hadis
Keeping alive opposition to foreign rule
Spreading Western scientific education among Muslims
q.x: Western education was the Aligarh aim; Deoband stood for traditional religious learning.

q.s: Who described the unification of India as the most notable achievement of British rule?
q.x: K.M. Panikkar held this view; unification and English as a link language helped nationalism grow.

q.s: The political method of the early Moderates in the Congress was:
q.x: The Moderates relied on prayers, petitions and protests; they never organised mass civil disobedience.

q.s: The Muslim League observed 22 December 1939 as the 'Day of Deliverance' to celebrate:
q.x: It marked the resignation of the Congress provincial ministries over the war issue.

q.s: The Muslim League raised the slogan 'Divide and Quit' at its 1943 session held at:
q.x: The slogan was raised at the Karachi session of 1943-44.

q.s: The longest-lasting parallel government during the Quit India Movement was set up at:
q.x: Satara's government lasted from mid-1943 to 1945-46; Ballia's lasted only about a week.

q.s: The 'Jatiya Sarkar', a parallel government of 1942, functioned at:
q.x: The Jatiya Sarkar of Tamluk (Midnapore) organised Vidyut Vahinis and cyclone relief.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a work by Mahatma Gandhi?
q.x: 'In Search of Gandhi' (1982) is by Richard Attenborough.

q.s: Who compared Gandhi's Dandi March to Napoleon's march on his return from Elba?
q.x: Subhas Chandra Bose made the comparison.

q.s: 'Generations to come will scarce believe that such a one as this ever walked upon this earth' was said about Gandhi by:
q.x: Albert Einstein paid this tribute to Gandhi.

q.s: The Congress Agrarian Reforms Committee of 1949, which set the land reform agenda, was headed by:
q.x: The Kumarappa Committee (1949) set the agenda; the Prakasam Committee (1938) had urged abolition of intermediaries.

q.s: The National Council for Land Reforms, set up in 2008, is chaired by the:
q.x: The Council was constituted on 9 January 2008 under the Prime Minister.

q.s: Which Justice Party leader, Chief Minister of Madras from 1932, opposed the separation of Andhra?
q.x: The Raja of Bobbili opposed separation; in 1938 the Wardha CWC assured the Andhra deputation.

q.s: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement (1956), recruitment to jobs in Telangana required a residence of:
q.x: The Agreement laid down 12 years' residence for recruitment in Telangana.

q.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956 provided:
o: Sharing of Krishna waters with Karnataka
Kurnool as the capital of Andhra
Safeguards for Telangana in the new Andhra Pradesh
q.x: It gave Telangana safeguards on revenue, jobs and education at the merger of 1956.

q.s: The States Reorganisation Commission (1953-55), which examined the Visalandhra question, was chaired by:
q.x: Fazl Ali chaired the SRC; Panikkar and Kunzru were its members.

q.s: Who was the last Chief Minister of undivided Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Kiran Kumar Reddy was the last CM before bifurcation in 2014.

q.s: Who succeeded Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy as Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in September 2009?
q.x: K. Rosaiah took over on 3 September 2009 after YSR died in a helicopter crash.

q.s: The Jai Andhra movement for a separate Andhra state took place in:
q.x: Jai Andhra (1972) was followed by the Six-Point Formula (1973).

q.s: The Girglani Commission (2001) was set up to examine:
o: The demand for a separate Telangana
Violations of GO 610 in public employment
q.x: The Girglani Commission looked into violations of GO 610 (1985) on local cadres.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act 2014, the existing admission quotas in educational institutions continue for ten years under Article:
q.x: Section 95 continues the quotas under Article 371D; Article 371E concerns a Central University.

q.s: The Thirteenth Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 deals with:
q.x: It lists education institutions and infrastructure measures to be taken within ten years (Section 93).

q.s: The Srikrishna Committee on the Telangana question submitted its report in:
q.x: The Srikrishna Committee reported in December 2010; 2001 is the year the TRS was founded.

q.s: The Telangana Rashtra Samithi (TRS) was founded in 2001 by:
q.x: K. Chandrasekhar Rao founded the TRS in April 2001.

q.s: The term 'Nigama-sabha' found in the Bhattiprolu inscription refers to a:
q.x: Nigama-sabha in the Bhattiprolu inscription means a town council.

q.s: Sriparvata (Vijayapuri), the capital of the Ikshvakus, is identified with:
q.x: Sriparvata-Vijayapuri is Nagarjunakonda in the Krishna valley.

q.s: According to Megasthenes, the Andhras had how many walled towns?
q.x: Megasthenes, whose account survives through Pliny, said the Andhras had 30 walled towns and a large army.

q.s: The principal coins of the Western Kshatrapas were made of:
q.x: Their principal coins were silver, numerous in western India; Kardamaka coins carry Saka-era dates.

q.s: 'Moturpha', a tax on trades and occupations such as looms, belongs to the:
q.x: Moturpha was a British-era tax; it is not a Satavahana term.

q.s: In Satavahana-period records, a 'nivartana' was a unit of:
q.x: A nivartana was a land unit of about 1.5 acres.

q.s: During the Satavahana period, the trade associations called Srenulu also functioned as:
q.x: Guilds accepted deposits and paid interest (about 12%), as the Nasik inscriptions show.

q.s: Bhutapala, a merchant of Vaijayanti, funded the great chaitya hall at:
q.x: The Karle chaitya was funded by Bhutapala.

q.s: Which of the following statements about donors to Satavahana-age Buddhist monuments is correct?
o: Guilds of goldsmiths were the main donors at Amaravati.
Only kings and ministers appear as donors.
Queens and women are prominent among the donors.
q.x: Women and queens head the donor lists; ivory workers' and other artisans' guilds also gave gifts.

q.s: The 108 Shiva temples called Narendreswara-alayas were built by the Eastern Chalukya king:
q.x: Vijayaditya II built them at the sites of his 108 battles with the Rashtrakutas, as recorded in the Sataluru inscription.

q.s: The Kalamalla inscription (c. 575 CE), regarded as the earliest Telugu inscription, was issued by the Renati Chola ruler:
q.x: Kalamalla is Dhanunjaya Varma's prose record, incomplete.

q.s: Which Renati Chola record is regarded as the first fully available Telugu inscription?
q.x: Erragudipadu is the first complete Telugu record; Kalamalla is incomplete.

q.s: The Renati Chola ruler Punyakumara bore the title:
q.x: Punyakumara was Pormukharama; Mahendra Vikramavarman was Muditha Silakshara Navarama.

q.s: The Kayastha chief defeated by Prataparudra II's commanders at Tripurantakam in 1291 was:
q.x: Ambadeva was defeated at Tripurantakam; Prataparudra stopped paying tribute to Delhi after Alauddin's death in 1316.

q.s: Under the Vijayanagara Amaranayaka system, the land assigned to a nayaka was called:
q.x: The Vijayanagara term was Amaram; Nayakasthalam was the Kakatiya term.

q.s: The Vijayanagara Amaranayaka system was a continuation of the Kakatiya:
q.x: Nayankara led to the Amaranayaka system and later to the Poligars.

q.s: Under the Ayagar system, each village had how many hereditary functionaries?
q.x: Each village had 12 hereditary Ayagars, among them the Kase (mason).

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Ayagar system?
o: They received a share of the village harvest
Ayagars were paid cash salaries by the state
q.x: Ayagars were paid through a harvest share and tax-free lands, not state salaries.

q.s: 'Parasara Madhaviyam', the authoritative law book of the Vijayanagara empire, was written by:
q.x: Madhavacharya's commentary on the Parashara Smriti was the authoritative law book; the Raya was the supreme judge.

q.s: Aliya Rama Raya, who was killed at Talikota in 1565, ruled as regent of:
q.x: Rama Raya was regent for Sadasiva Raya; his interference in Deccan politics united the Sultanates against him.

q.s: The bricks used in the vimana of the Ramappa temple are noted for being:
o: Light enough to float on water
q.x: Floating bricks reduce the dead weight of the tower.

q.s: The Ramappa temple, inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2021, was built under the:
q.x: Ramappa (Palampet) is a Kakatiya temple of the 13th century.

q.s: Which town became the first municipality in Andhra in 1861?
q.x: Bhimili became a municipality in 1861 under the British; the Dutch had left in 1825.

q.s: The Koh-i-Noor diamond is believed to have come from the mines of:
q.x: Kollur on the Krishna in Guntur district was a famous Golconda diamond mine.

q.s: 'Chintz', a major export of the early European trade from coastal Andhra, was a:
q.x: Chintz was a glazed, painted cotton cloth that became brighter after washing.

q.s: The Andhra Provincial Ryots Association was started in 1928 by:
q.x: N.G. Ranga started it; B.V. Ratnam was its first General Secretary, and it merged into the All India Kisan Sabha in 1936.

q.s: The All India Kisan Sabha was founded in 1936 at:
q.x: It was founded at Lucknow in April 1936; joint sessions were held with the Congress at Faizpur later that year.

q.s: The first president of the All India Kisan Sabha was:
q.x: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati was president and N.G. Ranga general secretary.

q.s: The Madras Public Libraries Act, the first library legislation in India, was passed in:
q.x: The Madras Act came in 1948; a bill had been moved in 1938.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh Public Libraries Act was passed in:
q.x: The AP Public Libraries Act was enacted in 1960.

q.s: The last Ikshvaku ruler, Rudrapurushadatta, was defeated by the:
q.x: The Pallava Simhavarman defeated him (Manchikallu inscription) and Pallava rule spread in the Krishna valley.

q.s: Kitab-ul-Yamini, an account of Mahmud of Ghazni's reign, was written by:
q.x: Utbi wrote Kitab-ul-Yamini; Baihaqi wrote Tarikh-i-Subuktigin.

q.s: Which of the following works was NOT written by Al-Biruni?
q.x: Taj-ul-Maasir is by Hasan Nizami, a chronicler of the Ghurid and early Sultanate period.

q.s: Muhammad Ghori suffered his first defeat in India in 1178 at the hands of the:
q.x: He was defeated at Kasahrada near Mount Abu, with queen mother Naika Devi as regent of Mularaja II.

q.s: In the Battle of Chandawar (1194), Muhammad Ghori defeated:
q.x: Ghori defeated the Gahadavala Jaichand at Chandawar near Firozabad.

q.s: According to Census 2011, India's work participation rate was:
q.x: The work participation rate in 2011 was 39.8%.

q.s: Which of the following statements based on Census 2011 is correct?
o: Punjab had the highest share of Hindus in its population.
The work participation rate was above 50%.
Agricultural labourers outnumbered cultivators for the first time.
q.x: 2011 was the first census in which agricultural labourers outnumbered cultivators; Himachal Pradesh had the highest Hindu share.

q.s: Divorce by mutual consent under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is provided under Section:
q.x: Section 13B covers mutual consent; Section 11 makes bigamous marriages void and Section 12 covers voidable marriages.

q.s: Under Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, a bigamous marriage is:
q.x: A bigamous marriage is void under Section 11.

q.s: 'Caste and Race in India' (1932), the first major sociological book on caste, was written by:
q.x: G.S. Ghurye wrote it in 1932; Risley was an earlier colonial ethnographer.

q.s: In south India, the demand for caste-based reservation was carried forward mainly by:
q.x: Periyar's Self-Respect Movement carried the demand in the south; the Satyashodhak Samaj worked in Maharashtra.

q.s: The shift of the Ezhavas of Kerala from toddy tapping to other trades is an example of:
q.x: Changing from a traditional caste occupation to a new one is occupational mobility.

q.s: In migration studies, failure of the monsoon in the area of origin acts as a:
q.x: Distress at the source pushes people out; higher urban wages are a pull factor.

q.s: After the Criminal Tribes Act was repealed in 1952, the communities it covered came to be called:
q.x: The repeal on 31 August 1952 made them Denotified Tribes.

q.s: The Criminal Tribes Act, branding about 200 communities as hereditary criminals, was first passed in:
q.x: The Act came in 1871; it was amended in 1924.

q.s: The Mizo National Front was led by:
q.x: Laldenga led the MNF and signed the Mizo Accord of 1986.

q.s: A.Z. Phizo led the:
q.x: Phizo led the NNC; Subhash Ghising led the GNLF.

q.s: Who defined casteism as 'an overriding, blind and supreme group loyalty'?
q.x: The definition is Kaka Kalelkar's; hostility to other castes marks casteism, not caste itself.

q.s: Hypergamy (anuloma marriage) is an exception to which feature of caste?
q.x: Among Ghurye's features of caste, anuloma is an exception to endogamy.

q.s: According to NCRB data for 2023, which State recorded the highest number of crimes against Scheduled Castes?
q.x: Uttar Pradesh recorded the most, ahead of Rajasthan.

q.s: The Anti-Arrack Movement of 1992 began in Dubagunta village of which district?
q.x: It began in Dubagunta, Nellore district, led by Dubagunta Rosamma and neo-literate women.

q.s: Prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs is a Directive Principle under Article:
q.x: Article 47 directs the State to bring about prohibition except for medicinal purposes.

q.s: The 'Study on Child Abuse: India 2007' was conducted by the:
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
Ministry of Women and Child Development
q.x: The Ministry of Women and Child Development conducted it; it found 53.22% of children reported sexual abuse.

q.s: As per NCRB data for 2023, which State recorded the highest number of crimes against children?
q.x: Madhya Pradesh had the highest number; Assam had the highest rate.

q.s: Under the Mines Act, 1952, no person may be employed in a mine below the age of:
q.x: The Mines Act bars persons below 18; the Factories Act, 1948 bars children below 14.

q.s: Which Directive Principle says that the tender age of children must not be abused?
q.x: Article 39(e) protects the tender age of children; 39(f) protects them against exploitation and abandonment.

q.s: The motto of the National Service Scheme (NSS) is:
q.x: NSS (1969) has the motto 'Not Me But You'; 'Unity and Discipline' is the NCC motto.

q.s: MY Bharat (Mera Yuva Bharat), launched on 31 October 2023, replaced the:
q.x: MY Bharat took the place of the NYKS.

q.s: The Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO) functions under the:
q.x: DMEO is an attached office of NITI Aayog.

q.s: The Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) Mission now functions under the:
q.x: The DBT Mission works under the Cabinet Secretariat.

q.s: The concept of 'backward mapping' in policy implementation was proposed by:
q.x: Elmore proposed backward mapping; Pressman and Wildavsky wrote the top-down study 'Implementation'.

q.s: The idea of 'street-level bureaucracy', stressing front-line officials in implementation, is associated with:
q.x: Lipsky's street-level bureaucracy is the classic bottom-up view.

q.s: Under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, prior government permission for layoff, retrenchment and closure is needed in establishments with at least:
q.x: The threshold was raised from 100 to 300 workers.

q.s: Under the new labour codes, fixed-term employees become eligible for gratuity after:
q.x: Fixed-term workers get gratuity after one year, against five years for regular employees.

q.s: The normal Centre-State funding ratio for Centrally Sponsored Schemes in general category States is:
q.x: CSS norm is 60:40; 90:10 for NE and Himalayan States and 100% for UTs without legislature.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Central Sector scheme?
q.x: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme; the other three are Central Sector.

q.s: 'NTR Bharosa' in Andhra Pradesh is a:
q.x: NTR Bharosa pensions reach about 61.92 lakh beneficiaries; AP tops up the central NSAP pension.

q.s: The Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan) was launched on:
q.x: It was launched on 3 December 2015, the International Day of Persons with Disabilities.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a vertical of the Accessible India Campaign?
q.x: The three verticals are built environment, transport and the ICT ecosystem.

q.s: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 replaced the:
q.x: The rights-based 2016 Act replaced the welfare-based 1995 Act; it came into force on 19 April 2017.

q.s: Which Indian served as President of the International Court of Justice during 1985-88?
q.x: Nagendra Singh was ICJ President in 1985-88.

q.s: In the Kulbhushan Jadhav case (2019), the ICJ held that Pakistan had violated the:
q.x: The ICJ found a breach of the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations.

q.s: An amendment of the UN Charter, needed for Security Council reform, must be ratified by two-thirds of the members including:
o: A majority of the permanent members
q.x: Under Article 108 all P5 must ratify, giving each a veto over reform.

q.s: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF), set up by the G7 in 1989, has its secretariat at:
q.x: The FATF secretariat is housed at the OECD in Paris.

q.s: In FATF usage, the list of 'jurisdictions under increased monitoring' is commonly called the:
q.x: The grey list is increased monitoring; the black list is high-risk jurisdictions subject to a call for action.

q.s: The Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act was enacted in:
q.x: AFSPA came in 1958; UAPA in 1967, TADA in 1985 and POTA in 2002.

q.s: Which of the following anti-terror laws was repealed in 2004?
q.x: POTA (2002) was repealed in 2004; TADA lapsed in 1995.

q.s: Which security force, raised in 1984, is popularly known as the 'Black Cats'?
q.x: The NSG is called the Black Cats; the SPG was formed in 1985.

q.s: The National Investigation Agency Act was enacted in 2008 following the:
q.x: The NIA Act came after the November 2008 Mumbai attacks.

q.s: In the three-tier coastal security system set up after 26/11, shallow coastal waters are patrolled by the:
q.x: The Navy has overall responsibility, the Coast Guard covers territorial waters and the Marine Police shallow waters.

q.s: The Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly was appointed on:
q.x: The Drafting Committee under Ambedkar was set up on 29 August 1947.

q.s: The Credentials Committee of the Constituent Assembly was chaired by:
q.x: Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar chaired the Credentials Committee.

q.s: Which committee of the Constituent Assembly was chaired by K.M. Munshi?
q.x: Munshi chaired the Order of Business Committee; Rajendra Prasad chaired the Steering and Finance and Staff Committees.

q.s: The Draft Constitution was moved for its first reading in the Constituent Assembly on 4 November 1948 by:
q.x: Dr B.R. Ambedkar moved the Draft Constitution.

q.s: At the final meeting of the Constituent Assembly, when members signed the Constitution and the National Anthem was adopted, the date was:
q.x: The final session met on 24 January 1950.

q.s: The method of election of the President of India was borrowed from the Constitution of:
q.x: Ireland gave the method of electing the President, the DPSPs and nomination to the Rajya Sabha.

q.s: The procedure for amending the Constitution was borrowed from:
q.x: South Africa gave the amendment procedure and the election of Rajya Sabha members.

q.s: The concept of 'procedure established by law' was borrowed from the Constitution of:
q.x: Procedure established by law is from Japan; 'due process' is the US idea.

q.s: Which of the following features is NOT correctly matched with its source?
o: Freedom of trade and commerce – Weimar Germany
Suspension of FRs in Emergency – Weimar Germany
Election of Rajya Sabha members – South Africa
q.x: Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse came from Australia.

q.s: For citizenship by naturalisation under the Citizenship Act, 1955, the general residence requirement is:
q.x: Naturalisation needs 12 years' residence (including the last 12 months) and an oath of allegiance.

q.s: A person of Indian origin ordinarily resident in India for 7 years can acquire Indian citizenship by:
q.x: The 7-year rule is for registration; marriage to a citizen is also a ground for registration.

q.s: Which of the following liberties is NOT mentioned in the Preamble?
q.x: The Preamble names five liberties: thought, expression, belief, faith and worship.

q.s: The word 'Secular' was added to the Preamble by the:
q.x: The 42nd Amendment added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity'.

q.s: In the Indian sense, secularism means:
o: Complete absence of religion in public life
q.x: Indian secularism means equal respect for all religions; the term is not defined in the Constitution.

q.s: Which judgment applied the creamy layer principle to reservation in promotions for SCs and STs?
q.x: Jarnail Singh applied creamy layer and dropped the need to prove SC/ST backwardness.

q.s: The Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 was renamed the Protection of Civil Rights Act in:
q.x: It was renamed by the 1976 amendment; 1989 is the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Article 17 is correct?
o: It was added by the 42nd Amendment.
It applies only against the State.
It applies against private individuals as well.
q.x: Article 17 binds private persons too; 'untouchability' is not defined in the Constitution.

q.s: The right to assemble under Article 19(1)(b) is available only if the assembly is:
q.x: Article 19(1)(b) protects peaceful assembly without arms.

q.s: In India, the right to strike is:
q.x: The Supreme Court (Kameshwar Prasad) held there is no fundamental right to strike.

q.s: Which writ is purely preventive, issued to stop a lower court from exceeding its jurisdiction?
q.x: Prohibition is preventive only; certiorari is both preventive and curative.

q.s: The writ of mandamus cannot be issued against:
q.x: Mandamus lies against public bodies but not against the President or a Governor.

q.s: In State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024), the Supreme Court held that States may:
q.x: A seven-judge bench held by 6:1 that States may sub-classify SCs.

q.s: The Davinder Singh judgment (2024) overruled which earlier decision?
q.x: It overruled E.V. Chinnaiah, which had barred sub-classification.

q.s: Article 23 of the Constitution prohibits:
o: Traffic in human beings and forced labour
q.x: Article 23 bans trafficking and begar; child employment in factories is Article 24.

q.s: Employment of children below 14 years in factories and mines is prohibited under Article:
q.x: Article 24 prohibits it.

q.s: National Legal Services Day is observed on:
q.x: It marks the coming into force of the Legal Services Authorities Act on 9 November 1995.

q.s: Free legal aid through NALSA and Lok Adalats gives effect to which Article?
q.x: Article 39A directs equal justice and free legal aid.

q.s: Which of the following Articles was NOT added by the 42nd Amendment?
q.x: Article 44 (uniform civil code) was in the original Constitution.

q.s: Article 38(2), on minimising inequalities in income, was added by the:
q.x: The 44th Amendment (1978) added Article 38(2).

q.s: The notice period for introducing a Private Member's Bill in Parliament is:
q.x: A Private Member's Bill needs a month's notice; a Government Bill needs seven days.

q.s: Rejection of which kind of bill in the Lok Sabha implies a loss of confidence in the government?
o: A bill referred to a Select Committee
A bill pending in the Rajya Sabha
q.x: Defeat of a Government Bill signals loss of confidence; a private member's bill has no such effect.

q.s: Which case struck down the 99th Constitutional Amendment and the NJAC Act?
q.x: The NJAC case struck them down 4:1 to protect judicial independence.

q.s: In which case did a nine-judge bench hold secularism and federalism to be basic features of the Constitution?
q.x: Bommai held secularism and federalism basic; Raj Narain was the first application of the doctrine.

q.s: Which motion need not state reasons and, if passed in the Lok Sabha, requires the Council of Ministers to resign?
q.x: A no-confidence motion needs no reasons; a censure motion must state reasons and does not force resignation.

q.s: A censure motion in the Lok Sabha differs from a no-confidence motion in that it:
o: Can be moved only in the Rajya Sabha
Must state the reasons for its adoption
q.x: A censure motion must give reasons and is only a disapproval of policies.

q.s: The Vice-President of India is elected by the:
o: Elected members of the Lok Sabha only
Members of both Houses of Parliament
Elected members of Parliament and State Assemblies
Members of the Rajya Sabha only
q.x: Under Article 66 only members of Parliament (elected and nominated) vote; State legislators do not.

q.s: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed by the President under Article:
q.x: Article 148 provides for the CAG; Article 360 is Financial Emergency and 280 the Finance Commission.

q.s: Under Article 143, the President may:
q.x: Article 143 gives the advisory jurisdiction; ordinances are under Article 123 and UT regulations under Article 240.

q.s: Under the President's pardoning power, a 'reprieve' means:
o: Awarding a lesser sentence for special reasons
Reducing the period of a sentence
q.x: Reprieve stays execution; respite is a lesser sentence for reasons like pregnancy.

q.s: Awarding a lesser sentence than the original because of a special fact, such as pregnancy of the convict, is called:
q.x: That is respite; remission shortens the period without changing the character of the sentence.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that a Governor cannot be removed merely because the Government at the Centre has changed?
q.x: B.P. Singhal held that the President's pleasure is not unfettered and removal must not be arbitrary.

q.s: The Governor of a State addresses his resignation to the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
q.x: He holds office during the President's pleasure and resigns to the President; under Art. 156(3) he continues until his successor takes over.

q.s: Under Article 200, the Governor must reserve for the President's consideration a Bill that:
o: Is passed by a bicameral legislature
Derogates from the powers of the High Court
q.x: A Bill that would endanger the High Court's position must be reserved.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Governor's options under Article 200 is correct?
o: The Constitution fixes no time limit for him to act.
He may withhold assent to a Bill passed again after return.
He may return a Money Bill for reconsideration.
He must decide on every Bill within one month.
q.x: No time limit is fixed in the text; a Money Bill cannot be returned and a Bill passed again must receive assent.

q.s: The Constitution (98th Amendment) Bill, 2003 proposed the creation of a:
q.x: The 2003 Bill proposed a National Judicial Commission for appointing judges.

q.s: Judicial review in India rests principally on the:
q.x: Judicial review flows from a written, supreme Constitution, federalism and Fundamental Rights.

q.s: The Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021 abolished the Film Certification Appellate Tribunal and transferred its appeals to the:
q.x: Cinematograph Act appeals now lie to the High Court; the NGT was not dissolved.

q.s: In Madras Bar Association v. Union of India (November 2025), the Supreme Court directed the Centre to set up a:
q.x: The Court gave four months to set up a National Tribunals Commission.

q.s: Article 1 of the Constitution describes India as a:
q.x: The word 'Federation' is not used anywhere in the Constitution.

q.s: The 16th Amendment (1963) allowed restrictions on free speech in the interest of:
q.x: The 16th Amendment added 'sovereignty and integrity of India'; public order and friendly relations came by the 1st Amendment.

q.s: Financial Emergency is provided for under Article:
q.x: Article 360 deals with Financial Emergency; 352 is National Emergency and 356 President's Rule.

q.s: 'Internal disturbance' as a ground for proclaiming a National Emergency was replaced by 'armed rebellion' by the:
q.x: The 44th Amendment (1978) made this change.

q.s: The Gadgil formula for distributing Plan assistance to States was first used for the:
q.x: It was introduced in 1969 for the Fourth Plan; the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula came in 1991 for the Eighth Plan.

q.s: The Gadgil formula gave the highest weight to:
q.x: Population carried 60 per cent weight.

q.s: The 14th Finance Commission was chaired by:
q.x: Y.V. Reddy chaired the 14th FC; it raised the States' share to 42%.

q.s: Which criterion was added for the first time by the 14th Finance Commission for sharing taxes among States?
q.x: It added forest cover (7.5%) and dropped fiscal discipline; income distance had the highest weight.

q.s: Election Commissioners can be removed from office by the President only on the recommendation of the:
q.x: The CEC is removed like a Supreme Court judge; other Commissioners only on the CEC's recommendation.

q.s: The Chairman and members of a Joint State Public Service Commission are appointed by the:
q.x: A Joint SPSC is created by Parliament on the request of the States; its members are appointed by, and resign to, the President.

q.s: A member of a State Public Service Commission holds office for six years or until the age of:
q.x: SPSC members serve six years or until 62; UPSC members until 65.

q.s: The CAG's audit reports on the accounts of a State are submitted to the:
q.x: Under Article 151(2) the reports go to the Governor, who lays them before the State Legislature.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Union Executive?
q.x: The Union Executive is the President, Vice-President, PM, Council of Ministers and Attorney General; the CAG is independent.

q.s: The reports of a State Commission for Women constituted under a State law are laid before the:
q.x: State commissions report to the State government, which lays the reports before the State Legislature.

q.s: How many members does the UN Human Rights Council have?
q.x: The Council has 47 members elected by the General Assembly, distributed among regional groups.

q.s: Which of the following statements about a State Human Rights Commission is correct?
o: Its Chairperson is appointed by the President.
It can only recommend compensation or action to the government.
Its recommendations are binding on the State government.
It can punish violators of human rights.
q.x: An SHRC is recommendatory; its members are appointed by the Governor.

q.s: The Right to Information Act, 2005 came fully into force on:
q.x: Enacted on 15 June 2005, it came fully into force on 12 October 2005; it turned 20 in 2025.

q.s: The RTI Online portal for central public authorities is run by the:
q.x: The DoPT runs the portal, since 2013.

q.s: Under the RTI Act, 2005, information concerning the life or liberty of a person must be supplied within:
q.x: Life or liberty information must be given within 48 hours.

q.s: The normal time limit for a Public Information Officer to reply under Section 7 of the RTI Act is:
q.x: The normal limit is 30 days; 45 days applies to human-rights allegations against Section 24 organisations.

q.s: The committee recommending the appointment of the Central Vigilance Commissioner consists of the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and the:
q.x: The CVC selection committee is PM, Home Minister and LoP; the CVC supervises the CBI in Prevention of Corruption Act cases.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Lokpal is correct?
o: It has no Inquiry Wing of its own.
It supervises the CBI only in cases it refers to the CBI.
Trials of its cases have no time limit.
It supervises the CBI in all corruption cases.
q.x: The Lokpal's superintendence over the CBI is limited to cases it refers; it has an Inquiry Wing and trials are to end within one year, extendable to two.

q.s: The Sixteenth Finance Commission (award period 2026-31) is chaired by:
q.x: Arvind Panagariya chairs the 16th FC; N.K. Singh chaired the 15th.

q.s: Actual devolution to States falls below the recommended 41% share mainly because a large part of gross tax revenue goes into:
q.x: About 18% of gross tax goes into cesses and surcharges, which are not shared, so actual devolution is about 31-32%.

q.s: Congress dominance of the Andhra Pradesh party system ended in 1983 with the victory of the:
q.x: N.T. Rama Rao's TDP won in 1983, ending Congress rule in AP.

q.s: Among the non-Congress governments formed after the 1967 elections, which State was governed by a single party rather than a coalition?
q.x: The DMK ruled Tamil Nadu alone; Bihar saw the most coalition governments.

q.s: The SVAMITVA scheme uses drone surveys to map properties in:
q.x: SVAMITVA gives property cards in village abadi areas, building a rural property-tax base.

q.s: AMRUT 2.0 (2021) is a scheme for:
q.x: AMRUT 2.0 is urban; it rewards property-tax reform and municipal bonds.

q.s: The State Finance Commission for Panchayats is provided for under Article:
q.x: 243I – State Finance Commission; 243K – State Election Commission; 243G – powers and functions.

q.s: How many subjects are listed in the Eleventh Schedule for devolution to Panchayats?
q.x: The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects; the Twelfth (municipalities) lists 18.

q.s: The 'triple test' for OBC reservation in local bodies, within the 50 per cent limit, was laid down in:
q.x: Gawali laid down the triple test: a dedicated commission, local-body-wise data, and the 50% cap.

q.s: In K. Krishna Murthy v. Union of India (2010), the Supreme Court held that political backwardness is:
o: A ground only for SC reservation
Distinct from social and educational backwardness
Identical to social and educational backwardness
q.x: The Court upheld Articles 243D(6) and 243T(6) and held political backwardness distinct.

q.s: In Fifth Schedule areas, regulations restricting the transfer of land by or among Scheduled Tribes are made by the:
q.x: Under Para 5 the Governor makes such regulations, with the President's assent.

q.s: In the Swiss-challenge method of public procurement, the process begins with:
q.x: A private party makes an unsolicited proposal; the government then invites counter-bids.

q.s: Under the Swiss-challenge method, the original proponent:
q.x: The right to match the best counter-bid is why it is criticised for information asymmetry.

q.s: In Halachmi's models of e-governance, putting government information in the public domain is called the:
q.x: Broadcasting disseminates information; critical flow sends critical information to a targeted audience such as an ombudsman.

q.s: The 'Make in India' initiative was launched on:
q.x: Make in India was launched on 25 September 2014; Startup India on 16 January 2016.

q.s: The Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan was announced in:
q.x: It was announced in May 2020, during the COVID-19 lockdown.

q.s: The Citizens Charter Bill, 2011, which sought to give statutory backing to citizens' charters:
o: Was struck down by the Supreme Court
q.x: It lapsed with the dissolution of the 15th Lok Sabha, so charters remain non-justiciable.

q.s: The 'Sevottam' model of the Government of India relates to:
q.x: Sevottam links citizens' charters, grievance redress and service delivery capability.

q.s: The SDG India Index is published by:
q.x: NITI Aayog publishes the SDG India Index; BRAP is by DPIIT and the Good Governance Index by DARPG.

q.s: The Good Governance Index is released by the:
o: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
q.x: DARPG brings out the Good Governance Index.

q.s: India's policy of non-alignment means:
o: Staying out of military blocs and judging issues on merits
An alliance with the Soviet bloc
q.x: Unlike passive neutrality, non-alignment is an active, independent stand without military alliances.

q.s: The Pattiseema lift irrigation scheme transfers Godavari water to the:
q.x: Pattiseema lifts Godavari water near Polavaram into the Polavaram right canal and on to the Prakasam barrage.

q.s: In the proposed Godavari-Cauvery link, the Krishna-Pennar segment runs from Nagarjunasagar to:
q.x: Godavari-Krishna: Inchampalli to Nagarjunasagar; Krishna-Pennar: Nagarjunasagar to Somasila; Pennar-Cauvery: Somasila to Grand Anicut.

q.s: The Tungabhadra Board was originally set up under the:
q.x: It was set up under Section 66 of the Andhra State Act, 1953; under APRA 2014 AP and Telangana replace undivided AP on it.

q.s: Red Sanders, endemic to the southern Eastern Ghats, grows mainly in the:
q.x: It grows in the Seshachalam, Veligonda, Lankamala, Nallamala and Talakona ranges of Chittoor and Kadapa.

q.s: Red Sanders is listed by the IUCN (2021) as:
q.x: Red Sanders is IUCN Endangered (2021).

q.s: Which is the only major port in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Visakhapatnam is the only major port; Krishnapatnam handles the most cargo among non-major ports.

q.s: After remeasurement at about 1,053 km, Andhra Pradesh's coastline ranks where among Indian States?
q.x: It is third, after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.

q.s: Jonnagiri, India's first private-sector gold mine, is located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Jonnagiri is in Kurnool district.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a beach-sand mineral found on the Andhra coast?
q.x: Bauxite occurs in the hills of Araku, Chintapalli and Paderu, not in beach sands.

q.s: The first WTO Ministerial Conference (1996) was held at:
q.x: MC1 was at Singapore (1996); MC3 at Seattle (1999) collapsed amid protests.

q.s: The 13th WTO Ministerial Conference (2024) was held at:
q.x: MC13 met at Abu Dhabi in 2024; MC11 was at Buenos Aires (2017).

q.s: The WTO Appellate Body has been non-functional since December 2019 because:
o: India withdrew from the dispute system
Its mandate expired under the Marrakesh Agreement
The USA blocked appointments of members
q.x: The US blocked new appointments, leaving it without a quorum.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the WTO dispute system is correct?
o: India was a founder member of the MPIA.
India has not joined the EU-led interim appeal arrangement (MPIA).
The Appellate Body has worked normally since 2020.
The MPIA was set up by the USA.
q.x: India stays out of the MPIA and wants the Appellate Body restored.

q.s: As per SRS 2024, which State has the highest share of elderly (60+) population?
q.x: Kerala has the highest elderly share.

q.s: As per SRS 2016-20, which State has the lowest life expectancy at birth?
q.x: Chhattisgarh has the lowest; NCT Delhi has the highest.

q.s: The Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (1989) was formed by merging NREP and:
q.x: JRY merged NREP and RLEGP; TRYSEM was a self-employment training scheme.

q.s: DWCRA, launched in 1982 for rural women, was a sub-scheme of:
q.x: DWCRA was a sub-scheme of the Integrated Rural Development Programme.

q.s: The first Aadhaar numbers were issued in 2010 at Tembhli village in:
q.x: Tembhli is in Nandurbar district of Maharashtra.

q.s: The idea of the JAM trinity was first put forward in the:
q.x: The Economic Survey 2014-15 proposed linking Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and Mobile; the bank account is the destination of funds.

q.s: The new national accounts series with base year 2022-23 benchmarks private final consumption expenditure on the:
q.x: PFCE is benchmarked on HCES 2022-23; the series uses double deflation and Supply and Use Tables.

q.s: Which NSO survey covers registered factories?
q.x: ASI covers registered factories; ASUSE covers unincorporated non-agricultural enterprises.

q.s: Which survey provides the weights for the Consumer Price Index?
q.x: The Household Consumption Expenditure Survey gives CPI weights; PLFS measures employment.

q.s: From January 2025, the PLFS began releasing monthly all-India unemployment estimates based on the:
q.x: The revamped PLFS gives monthly CWS estimates and extended quarterly estimates to rural areas.

q.s: In the Human Development Index, the standard of living is measured by:
q.x: The HDI uses the logarithm of GNI per capita in PPP dollars.

q.s: The HDI takes the logarithm of income because income contributes to human development with:
q.x: Each extra dollar adds less to human development.

q.s: Which index adjusts the HDI for inequality in health, education and income?
q.x: The Inequality-adjusted HDI discounts the HDI for inequality, which national averages hide.

q.s: The last expert group on poverty estimation set up by the Planning Commission was headed by:
q.x: The Rangarajan group (2012) reported in 2014.

q.s: The Tendulkar Expert Group on poverty estimation submitted its report in:
q.x: Set up in 2005, it reported in December 2009.

q.s: Among social groups in India, the highest poverty ratio in 2011-12 was among the:
q.x: STs had the highest poverty ratio, about 43-45%.

q.s: India's social protection coverage, as reported by the ILO in 2025, rose to about:
q.x: Coverage rose from 22% in 2016 to 64.3% in 2025.

q.s: The Environmental Kuznets Curve, relating environmental degradation to per capita income, has the shape of:
q.x: Degradation rises with income up to a threshold and then falls.

q.s: The original Kuznets curve relates per capita income to:
q.x: Kuznets proposed that inequality first rises and then falls as income grows.

q.s: Disguised unemployment in India is found mainly in:
q.x: Seasonal and disguised unemployment are mainly rural; educated unemployment is mainly urban.

q.s: Which type of unemployment can exist even at full employment?
